vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: central-intelligence
Version: 1.0.0

The skill implements a persistent memory system that directs the agent to exfiltrate session context, project decisions, and environment details to an external third-party API (central-intelligence-api.fly.dev). It also instructs the agent to prompt the user to execute an unverified remote package (npx central-intelligence-cli) for account setup. While these actions are aligned with the stated goal of providing long-term memory, the automated collection of environment data and the centralization of sensitive agent context on an external platform represent significant privacy and supply-chain risks.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (persistent memory) matches its runtime behavior (calls a remote memory API), but there are metadata inconsistencies and instructions that can cause automatic cross-session data sharing and potential sensitive-data leakage — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md implements a remote persistent-memory service accessed via an API key (CI_API_KEY), which is coherent with the skill's stated purpose. However the registry metadata (no required env vars, no homepage) contradicts the SKILL.md which declares CI_API_KEY required and includes a homepage/repo. That mismatch reduces trust and is unexpected for a skill that relies on an external service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions direct the agent to always run a 'context' recall at session start, to remember environment details, and to support cross-scope sharing (agent→user→org). Those behaviors can cause automatic loading and propagation of stored information across sessions and agents, increasing risk of accidental exposure of sensitive information. The SKILL.md also tells users to run `npx central-intelligence-cli signup` to obtain an API key — a command that would execute code from the npm registry if run, so users should treat it cautiously. Apart from the API requests to the documented base URL, the instructions do not ask the agent to read other local files or other environment variables.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files, so nothing is written to disk by the skill itself. The SKILL.md suggests obtaining an API key via `npx central-intelligence-cli signup` (user-executed), which would fetch/run an npm package; that is outside the skill but worth flagging as a potential vector the user must manually trust.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Functionally the skill only requires a single API key (CI_API_KEY), which is proportionate to calling a remote memory service. However the registry metadata omitted this required env var while SKILL.md lists it, an inconsistency that reduces confidence. Also, because memories can be shared across agent/user/org scopes, storing secrets, tokens, or sensitive system details in memories would be dangerous — the documentation even suggests remembering environment details, which could unintentionally include sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always:false) and model invocation is allowed (default). The instruction to 'Always run context at session start' combined with normal autonomous invocation increases the chance the agent will automatically fetch and act on persisted memories each session. This is expected for a memory skill but raises privacy/exfiltration considerations if sensitive data is stored.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill talks to a remote memory API and requires a CI_API_KEY — only install if you trust the external service and owner. Before enabling: (1) verify the repository/homepage and owner identity (registry metadata mismatch is suspicious); (2) do not store secrets, passwords, or private keys as 'memories'; treat stored memories as potentially readable by other agents if you use user/org sharing; (3) avoid running the suggested `npx central-intelligence-cli signup` unless you trust the npm package and have inspected it; (4) consider creating a dedicated, limited-scope API key (or test key) and try with non-sensitive dummy data first; (5) if you need stricter control, ask for the skill to remove the 'always run context at session start' directive or to require explicit user consent before loading/sharing memories.
